claims.statement: Activity islands share a 28-point collapsed height and minimum 72-point width. Compact and expanded widths are measured from actual content and rounded to the shared 8-point grid, without fixed 208-point or 288-point minimums.
Activity-island width and height use one 240 ms cubic ease-out transition, preserving the visible size on reversal and applying target geometry directly for reduced motion.

Only one activity expands at a time. Paired activities use equal fixed slots and a 6-point gap, keeping their inner anchors stable across selection and metric digit changes. They expand outward within their respective half of the available space; a single activity stays centered and smaller tiers are used if the complete detail grid cannot fit.

Activity content keeps a fixed drawable at the native window origin with a sibling rounded mask; details retain their full-width layout, and secondary header fields appear only after they fit beside the persistent main value.

Conversation spacing uses 20 points between messages and around the 24-point work status, and 6 points between a completed process header and its answer; the composer contributes 8 points to the lower gap.

The composer uses a theme-accent Ultrafast glyph and opens its model popover only with a nonempty current catalog. A known model remains visible during catalog refresh or failure; otherwise the closed control uses a hyphen without a selection prompt. Suggestions wrap in the normal editor, and quotes appear only in new conversations without history.

The automated native activity probe runs 20 Work and Debug transitions with four interrupted openings, checks foreground origin and viewport geometry, and requires no daemon or model request; its trace measures CPU draw and submission rather than GPU completion or scanout.
Repository instructions require all activity islands to reuse the shared geometry and motion contract and require new variants to update that contract and its focused checks.

A confirmed-empty personal Assistant topic shows the centered 20-point heading What’s next? and the same-Assistant explanation; a new project Agent shows What would you like to do? and its project chooser.

The shared empty-conversation start heading yields to saved history, sending previews, retained failed or unconfirmed input, active work, questions, and misalignment; missing or unavailable history retains its existing loading or retry presentation.

A missing selected working directory is presented as an unavailable working folder with a restoration instruction; generic connection admission failures use Reconnecting to Codex while account readiness failures keep their specific Accounts guidance.

The isolated native stream recovery test drops the first local SSE response before completion and proves that retry preserves the original running thread and turn, completes normally, and does not enqueue a duplicate input.

The sidebar uses 28-point rows, 12.5-point normal body-color conversation and project labels, and 12.5-point medium primary-color category and Archived labels, with 5-point row corners. Expanded open project groups add 8 points of space while closed headers and compact groups add none; empty explanations use one ordinary expanded row and no compact row. Divider slots use 12 points. Quiet expanded conversations and completed ones with no unread result leave the shared leading slot empty. Compact conversation rows show their first complete grapheme with shared state ink. Marked expanded rows retain the same title column. Times and shortcuts use 10.5-point captions.
Human attention is derived from pending native requests, unanswered native questions and explicit user-decision state rather than displayed labels; ordinary returned agent work is separate.
Window controls retain fixed-size icons without visible toolbar labels; Collaboration shows pending count in a small badge while keeping its name in the tooltip and accessibility label.

Conversation rows reveal three inline actions on hover or keyboard focus: Pin or Unpin, Archive, and Delete. Archived rows reveal only Restore and Delete. Delete first arms confirmation with red ink and the shared icon nudge, then confirms on the second click. The 24-point target stays fixed. Pointer departure, Escape, or an outside click cancels. Hints supply short action names, confirmation or disabled reasons. Selected conversation and draft remain unchanged during confirmation.

The compact sidebar retains a full-height 40-point rail, category symbols, project and conversation initials and a fixed command entry. A 100 ms hover expands it temporarily, including after automatic collapse; departure waits 220 ms and reentry cancels departure. Operating a category or project disclosure during a hover does not pin it. A hover preview clips only the overlap with Collaboration and keeps the uncovered content visible and interactive at its existing size and position.

Overflowing sidebar titles use hover or keyboard-focus motion by default, each section can opt into continuous scrolling, and leaving the hover returns the label through the shared tween with reduced-motion support.

The sidebar tooltip anchors to the complete row through shared adaptive hover placement, keeping the row and its action hit targets uncovered. It shows owner and update time, plus active status when available and the title in the compact rail.

During sidebar opening, closing and reversal, content retains the complete expanded width and remains mounted while the outer panel clips the shared width transition. The settled 40-point rail exposes category symbols and project or conversation initials. Text is not squeezed into intermediate widths or removed when the target first changes.

HoverIntent owns the shared 100 ms entry dwell, 220 ms departure grace and pending cancellation for the sidebar, activity islands, response-statistics popover and history previews. The history group and card form one target; scrubbing changes content immediately without repeating arrival.

Committed hover intent and explicit surface toggles grant a bounded 400 ms animation window in a visible inactive App without changing the background-rendering preference; ordinary background policy resumes after expiry, and system reduced motion and VoiceOver still suppress motion.

Sidebar text retains its complete shaping, text, color and position behind a shared Viewport mask measured from actual pane bounds. The visible edge reveals or covers it without a per-label fade, character counter or reveal clock. Leading slots remain fixed, reversals change current clipping geometry, and reduced motion resolves directly.

The main macOS window leaves traffic_light_position unset and uses an AppKit unified compact toolbar; GPUI places its top control groups at the measured native control-row center instead of moving native window buttons or their containers.

Control groups share the 28-point height, 24-point targets, 4-point inner spacing and gap, 8-point outer inset and capsule radius, and 5-point small-control radius; attached material surfaces preserve their allocated anchor, while independent floating menus use the shared 8-point edge clearance.
Work and Debug headers reserve a 14-point waveform or performance-gauge symbol plus a 6-point gap, include that slot in measured sizing, and tint the symbols with the active accent color.

The main window minimum is 480 by 360 points. Panel allocation reserves 360 points for reading and prioritizes left navigation independently of opening order. A nonfitting right panel floats; nonfitting full navigation returns to its rail and retains its pinned preference for wider windows.

Both sidebars use the original workspace_surface and workspace field color in the main GPUI window for docked, floating and compact states, without separate native Liquid Glass surfaces. Shared clipping and overlay dismissal preserve the existing editor and responsive layout.

Work in progress projects unfinished tasks and observed native agents from the current conversation subtree when Graph is hidden; it reuses disclosure motion, opens existing conversations, and constrains its scrolling list to one quarter of window height between two and six 28-point rows.
Panel placement state comes from open workspace allocation and remains docked or floating through closing and reversal; it governs allocation and dismissal without selecting a different material.

When Overlay glass style has no saved override it inherits Window glass style, including later changes, while an explicit Regular or Clear choice remains independent and inheritance creates no stored override.

workspace_panel_content supplies a shared system font, 12.5-point body size and 19-point line height without a background fill. Workspace panels keep their clipping transition and omit native menu opacity and vertical entrance effects.

The main-window sidebar routes pointer entry and departure through one shared HoverIntent owner in expanded and compact states. Entry starts the shared dwell even when the pointer stops without another unpressed mouse move.

Sidebar reveal geometry comes from the main window. ui_layout::pane reuses unchanged content there, while state, activity and hover changes invalidate it and active accessibility retains live semantic geometry. Input bars, activity islands and menus retain their separate native material behavior.
Native clipped surfaces update material and foreground mask geometry in one Core Animation transaction with implicit actions disabled and skip unchanged clipping geometry.

The visual-capture binary has an opt-in display-backed native workspace probe. With explicit trace and isolated draft paths, it exercises 12 left, right and combined transitions including reversals, uses the existing Graph fixture and process-local appearance preferences, and records CPU frame timing and rebuild counts without a live service.

The compact rail and temporary navigation preview retain their full height and bottom Archived footer during opening, closing and automatic collapse. An explicitly pinned full navigation panel that must float, and the right floating panel, stop above the complete composer area. Floating panels mask covered reading-plane paint and hit regions without reflow.

The native composer measures content at its current parent anchor width and uses one selected native material without an additional GPUI fill or window backdrop, while retaining the editor and its focus.

The visual capture binary's DECODEX_VISUAL_NATIVE_COMPOSER mode resizes a real AppKit composer and toggles a workspace panel with an isolated draft root and process-local appearance, recording native rendering dimensions without a live service.

Both sidebars use revealed_value to set the lower edge before opening into a known floating placement; later height changes animate only while the panel is already visible, preserving closing and reversal continuity.

A full-height navigation preview masks only the covered portion of the native composer composite and its pointer region. Its material contour, foreground size and draft remain intact. Focusing the composer dismisses the preview.

The workspace samples left and right layout slots and visible widths together in one PanelFrame. Sidebars and content masks reuse the painted geometry through opening, closing and reversal. The native composer applies that frame's mask during parent prepaint before paint, while retaining its existing material and editor.
The idle Work header does not reserve or render a hidden generation-rate field. Header and detail measurement retain actual metric values and a legible compact sparkline.

History previews retain two input lines and three reply lines with a shared separator. Input and reply use the same normal theme body color, font size, weight and line height. Compact body text uses 12/18-point size/line height. Sidebar time and compact conversation metrics share ui_theme::metric_text and metric_ink: normal 10.5/14-point caption text, tabular figures and muted ink at 85%. ui_time owns relative age, timestamps and duration formatting, and work-level duration delegates to it. Whole seconds omit .0; durations from one day use days and remaining hours. Recorded zero duration is 0s and missing is an em dash. Fixed vector symbols do not depend on the text font. The metadata row retains five equal-width centered columns; footprints precede known step counts including zero, an em dash if unknown and an ellipsis while running. Full step wording remains available to accessibility. Ordinary recorded counts add no hint; unknown, running and terminal-state explanations remain available. Value length and missing data preserve column allocation. The final excerpt and metric row are separated by 8 points through ui_theme::METRIC_GROUP_GAP, with no second divider.

Persistent floating controls use MaterialSurface with Overlay material and Overlay glass style. Its opacity affects the native window composite, including material and foreground. An owner-controlled fade does not also run the native entrance effect, and the control owner hides the attached window when the control leaves the current view.

Pin, Assistant and Projects retain theme-owned symbol colors in palette slots 3, 0 and 1, including compact presentation. Projects uses a filled native folder; expanded individual projects and project command results use neutral outline folders. Compact projects use neutral name initials. Project IDs do not select colors. Selection and conversation activity retain existing semantic colors, with shared state ink applied to compact conversation initials.

Group previews use Popover::hover_preview with the complete trigger group as their anchor and the common adaptive hover placement policy. Timeline previews keep a fixed 320-point width. First presentation uses the measured final height; later height changes use the shared 200 ms interruptible Tween and preserve continuity on reversal. Text stays at its measured size behind the changing frame. Native and GPUI hosts share placement and height policy, with 8-point edge clearance and direct target resolution for reduced motion. Ordinary menus retain their placement and fixed-size arrival.

Process and complete Live disclosures share conversation_divider geometry. Process uses the shared 11-point normal muted metric caption in a 20-point row; Section uses 12.5-point semibold primary text in a 24-point row. Both retain the shared leading chevron, full-height control and fading hairline. A folded Live source preview is replaced by the expanded transcript. The shared 6-point content gap follows the divider, speaker turns use the 20-point reading gap, and the shared 4-point metadata gap precedes the response footer.

Ordinary reply and Live footers share Time, Input, Output and Spend components and one details popover. Spend uses the common USD formatter and coin symbol, estimates use an approximation mark, partial estimates append a plus sign, and unknown values remain distinct from recorded zero. These response fields leave the five-column history-preview layout intact.

Hover hints add icon-only action names, shortcuts, hidden values, failure reasons or estimate inputs. Expanded navigation utility labels, normal step counts, visible answer options and Live Mute/Unmute or End/Cancel labels suppress duplicate hints. Compact project names and hidden directories remain available.

GPUI text callers use HoverHint::hover_hint and anchored metadata uses tooltip_at. The common builder owns interface typography at 12/18 points, horizontal/vertical insets of 8/6 points, a 360-point maximum width, a 10-point corner radius and the shared half-point outline. Text hints fit the smallest width that preserves the line count at maximum width, removing unused trailing space without adding lines or changing text. Callers supply content without separate feature chrome.

Passive GPUI hints reuse Overlay material and glass-style preferences in a separate bounded native host per parent. Foreground is measured in the framework tooltip slot and rendered once in a window that ignores pointer input and never requests focus. Framework dwell/lifetime, owner release, explicit popup opening and application activation govern dismissal. Native tooltip anchors and interactive popup hosts use the shared MouseExited observer to clear GPUI's retained in-window pointer position, preventing stale child-window hover. Focused checks cover dwell, removal, pointer actions, wrapping and native departure semantics.

SwiftUI menu-bar controls use one HoverHint adapter with the existing Overlay preference keys, a 500 ms dwell and a passive material panel. It supports key nonactivating status panels, cancels stale owners and input, and removes duplicate quota and completed/reset-progress text while retaining hidden error and confirmation information.

Hover hints and detail previews anchor to the complete trigger bounds rather than the current cursor. Shared placement keeps an 8-point trigger gap and edge clearance, tries below, above, right and left, and uses the first fitted candidate that clears the trigger and its gap. Native windows use the screen's visible bounds, including space outside the small composer window; the GPUI fallback uses window bounds. SwiftUI HoverHint applies the same rule in screen coordinates.
The SwiftUI HoverHint adapter measures compact text width while preserving the original maximum-width height, so wrapped path hints release unused trailing space without adding lines.

Pin, Assistant and Projects are independently collapsible categories in one scrolling directory. Each project expands independently so several projects and their conversations remain visible together. Category, project and conversation labels share one text column after a single 28-point leading slot, without tree guides or accumulating indentation. Search stays above the directory and Archived stays at the bottom. Pin adds shortcuts without removing source membership.

Project disclosures open and close their own conversation groups without changing the selected conversation or closing other projects. Category disclosure preserves open-project choices. Sorting and creation controls share pointer-hover and keyboard-focus visibility and a width/opacity transition; hidden controls release title space. An open options menu keeps its controls visible. Disclosures retain a fixed trailing position. Expanded empty groups show one ordinary explanation row; compact groups omit explanation rows and group spacing, and Archived uses the category style and shared disclosure above a fixed bottom divider. Group geometry uses shared intrinsic disclosure and chevron motion on the continuous sidebar surface.

Category and project expansion choices belong to the current window. The directory and archive browser retain separate scroll handles. Opening a conversation through Search and commands expands and reveals its category and project without closing other projects. Tests exercise independent expansion, common text origins, fixed Search and Archived controls, cross-project draft restoration, pin shortcuts, empty unsent editor exclusion and deletion cancellation.

Sidebar artwork uses native SF Symbols through workspace_symbols. Category, project and sorting icons use 16 points. The creation symbol and the expanded conversation mark frame use 14 points. Disclosure symbols use 12 points. The sorting symbol uses arrow.up.arrow.down. Rows retain a 28-point height with 28-point leading slots and 24-point small action areas. The shared macOS generator supplies the artwork, and visible-alpha checks cover the embedded templates.

Project headers reveal Delete project beside New conversation on hover or keyboard focus. The first click arms the fixed 24-point delete target with red ink and the shared ConfirmationNudge; the second removes the project. Pointer departure, Escape, or an outside click cancels. The confirmation hint says chats and files remain. No separate deletion menu or confirmation panel is used.

The compact sidebar uses a 28-point leading symbol column between equal 6-point insets in its 40-point rail. Category, project, conversation and utility labels start at the clipped edge, avoiding partial letters while keeping symbols centered; trailing action targets remain 24 points.

Compact project and conversation rows show the first complete Unicode grapheme in the centered 28-point leading slot, preserving combined accents, Chinese characters and emoji. Category and utility icons remain; expanded full titles keep normal weight. The shared RailInitial owns the character extraction and typography.

Expanded sidebar rows show three opacity-pulsed dots for running conversations and steady dots with reduced motion. Amber attention and red failure rings share their 6-point diameter with the filled blue unread-result dot. Status marks carry accessible state labels.

A pending result in the sidebar takes priority over the conversation's base status. Explicitly opening the conversation and loading its available history acknowledges the exact result selected on open.

The Timeline rail is centered at the minimum 24-point gap between the message edge and trailing workspace edge. Its center retains a fixed 12-point trailing inset in wider layouts. The 16-point rail extends its hit target into the workspace gutter and clips covered parts to the shared reading-plane mask.
